title: Smart Vacuum Cleaner
subtitle: ESP8266 & WiFi Joystick Controlled Cleaning Robot with Relay Air Pump
desc: A smart robotic vacuum cleaner powered by ESP8266 WiFi NodeMCU, featuring a 5V Relay Air Pump switch, proportional Virtual Touch Joystick navigation, dual STA/AP modes, and mDNS web dashboard.
fullDesc: The Smart Vacuum Cleaner Robot is built upon the popular 3D printable chassis designed by Marcus Lanzoni (Thingiverse #5116129). Powered by an ESP8266 NodeMCU microcontroller, the robot connects seamlessly via local WiFi (STA mode) or creates its own Access Point (VacuumBot-AP). Users can control the robot in real-time through an interactive web dashboard accessed at http://vacuum.local/ or IP address. The web app features a smooth 2D Virtual Joystick where motor speed increases proportionally as the stick is pushed further out from center, along with a dedicated relay switch for the vacuum suction air pump and detailed live JSON diagnostic telemetry.
author: Umeshwari Baviskar
innovation: Combines a 3D printed vacuum chassis (Thingiverse #5116129) with ESP8266 WiFi remote control, smooth touch virtual joystick vector steering, proportional displacement speed scaling, relay air pump switching, and mDNS zero-configuration web access.
problemStatement: Manual cleaning robots often lack intuitive remote control and telemetry visibility. Providing a smooth touch joystick interface with variable speed and dedicated relay suction pump control makes floor cleaning educational and highly efficient.
solutionApproach: An ESP8266 NodeMCU controls an L298N/L293D motor driver and a 5V/12V relay module connected to a high-speed vacuum suction air pump. The onboard web server renders a smooth HTML5 Canvas Virtual Joystick that maps 2D touch vectors directly to differential motor speeds, while serving rich JSON diagnostics at /status.

hardwareSpecs.vacuumPump: 12V High-Speed DC Suction Fan / Air Pump

components: 3D Printed Vacuum Chassis (Thingiverse #5116129 by Marcus Lanzoni)
12V DC High-Speed Air Vacuum Pump / Fan
guide: Step 1: 3D print the Marcus Lanzoni chassis components (Thingiverse #5116129).
Step 2: Assemble the drive motors, wheels, caster wheel, and dust filtration chamber.
Step 3: Connect the 5V Relay module signal pin to ESP8266 D4 (GPIO2) to trigger the vacuum air pump.
Step 4: Wire the L298N motor driver inputs to ESP8266 D1, D2, D6, D7, D5 (ENA), D8 (ENB).
Step 5: Connect the battery pack power distribution to the motor driver, relay, and ESP8266 VIN pin.
Step 6: Open vacuumrobo.ino in Arduino IDE with ESP8266 board support installed.
Step 7: Upload the code and open Serial Monitor at 115200 baud.
Step 8: Connect your phone or laptop to WiFi 'STEM' or 'VacuumBot-AP' (Password: 12345678).
Step 9: Open browser and navigate to http://vacuum.local/ or IP address.
Step 10: Toggle the Vacuum Air Pump Relay ON and use the Virtual Joystick to clean!
